correction_pass_2026_11_01c.trigger: parent-investigator check: does the weak-neuter bridge wrongly insert an oblique -an- stem before the nasalized ending?
correction_pass_2026_11_01c.finding: Yes, the prior correction pass's candidate PGmc *erþa-kunþan-oN was wrong. Re-checked Fulk's own guma (masc. n-stem) and augo (neut. n-stem) paradigm tables (p.168, already held, re-read only, no new search): the -an-/-n- element is present from the ACCUSATIVE singular onward in masc. n-stems (nom. guma, but acc./gen./dat. guman) and only in the PLURAL of neut. n-stems (sg. augo/ēage with no -n- at all; pl. augona/ēagan with -n-). The nominative/accusative-syncretic neuter singular therefore takes the ending directly on the bare stem, with no inserted -an-. Corrected candidate: PGmc *erþa-kunþ-oN (bare compound stem + nasalized ending), CAPR notation *erþa-kunthing-with-nasal-o, i.e. the same final syllable as an earlier literal (pre-nasalization-correction) -ON experimental input already reported successful by the parent, now simply with the nasalization corrected -- not the -anoN shape, which duplicates the distinct ACCUSATIVE masc. serialization *-anoN and is not the right parallel for this nominative/accusative-syncretic neuter cell.
correction_pass_2026_11_01c.correction_made: morphology.md technical note and Recommendation item 1 rewritten to give PGmc *erþa-kunþ-oN (no -an-) as the corrected inference, with the erroneous -an- insertion flagged and explained via the guma/augo paradigm tables.

correction_pass_2026_11_01d.trigger: Parent flagged suspected circumflex(trimoric)-to-macron(bimoric) notation conflation in the weak-neuter PGmc bridge *erþa-kunþ-ōⁿ, plus a replay finding that PGmc *-aimiz does not derive attested dat.pl -um (yields -em instead).
correction_pass_2026_11_01d.method: Re-rendered Fulk scan pp.186-187 (printed pp.169-170) at 260dpi (pdftoppm -r 260 -png); cropped and visually compared the specific glyphs in: (a) "Only *-o or *-on will account for the WGmc. masc. forms" (confirmed circumflex, caret-shaped accent), (b) "Likewise, *-o is required to explain Go. neuter -o," (first -o circumflex/PGmc reconstruction, second -o plain macron/attested Gothic spelling, not a reconstruction), (c) "whereas the neuter endings in the other languages require *-on;" (confirmed MACRON, flat-bar accent, not circumflex), (d) "PIE neuter *-on," (macron). Calibrated against an unambiguous same-page example mixing both diacritics explicitly ("*-e, *-e[circumflex], or *-e[circumflex]n") to confirm the renderer/font reliably distinguishes the two shapes at this resolution.
correction_pass_2026_11_01d.finding: The earlier draft of morphology.md had MISQUOTED the WGmc/ON neuter nom./acc.sg ending as circumflex *-on[circumflex] (apparently by contamination from the immediately adjacent, genuinely-circumflex masculine and Gothic-neuter clauses in the same sentence). On pixel-level re-verification, Fulk explicitly prints this specific (WGmc/ON, i.e. the OE-relevant) neuter ending with a MACRON: *-on with a flat bar, i.e. bimoric nasalized. This means the previously-used CAPR bridge *erθa-kunth-oN (CAPR notation *érθa-kùnðǭ, bimoric ǭ) is NOT a bimoric/trimoric conflation: it faithfully transcribes Fulk's own printed macron ending for the correct (WGmc/ON) branch. The genuinely-circumflex (trimoric) forms in this passage belong to a DIFFERENT cell (WGmc masculine nom.sg) and to the Gothic-specific neuter derivation, not to the WGmc/ON neuter cell used for the weak-neuter candidate.
correction_pass_2026_11_01d.residual_uncertainty: The parent independently inspected the printed glyph and paragraph: Fulk's 'perplexing' qualifies the preceding WGmc masculine trimoric origin, not the OE-relevant bimoric neuter ending. Fulk gives an inherited PIE account for the latter and cites Boutkan's analogical-from-neuter-plural alternative. That competing prehistory remains explicit; the whole accented compound is CAPR's comparative assembly, not Fulk's printed whole word. No invented trimoric-to-bimoric transition or resolution of the whole paradigm is required for this neuter cell.
correction_pass_2026_11_01d.dat_pl_qualification: Per parent's replay (not independently re-run within this bounded philological thread): PGmc *-aimiz does not derive attested OE -um under the current diphthong-coding, yielding -em instead (eorþcundem/godcundem). The complete dative ending remains unresolved. Unlike the dative, the correctly bimoric Genesis weak-neuter input is accepted by the production parser and completely succeeds with general medial prominence.

final_synthesis_2026_11_01.preferred_cell: Attested Genesis A 1627 weak neuter accusative singular eorþcunde, from CAPR-assembled *érθa-kùnðǭ under Fulk's inherited n-stem account and the general medial-prominence hypothesis.
final_synthesis_2026_11_01.source_verification: Fulk 2018 pp.168-170, 216-217 and Campbell §§638,656 support the morphological bridge, ending and poetic syntax. The final original-glyph rendering was independently inspected by the integrating investigator; no copyrighted image is committed.
final_synthesis_2026_11_01.documentary_limit: Three distinct dictionary-located occurrences recovered versus six reported DOEC tokens. Thorpe's OCR supports the Genesis location/syntax, not exact printed thorn/eth or hyphenation; manuscript and critical apparatus remain uncollated.
final_synthesis_2026_11_01.fallback: Strong masculine/neuter genitive *eorþcundes from *érθa-kùnðas remains regularly derived experimentally and unattested in the recovered evidence.
final_synthesis_2026_11_01.experiment_label_correction: The rejected trimoric nasal trial was prompted by a superseded source misreading, not Fulk's actual OE-neuter ending. V11 corrects its label while preserving the authentic v10 record and all predictions.
